title: Switch on a String code

blocks.text: A `switch` on a `String` compares with `equals()`, so the match is case-sensitive. A `null` selector throws `NullPointerException`, so it is handled before the switch (or, since Java 21, with a `case null` label).
A warehouse labels fruit with two-letter codes, in capitals. Write `name(String code)` in `Codes`:
Codes are exact: `"ap"` is not a code, so `name("ap")` is `"unknown"`.

cases.says: AP, BN and CH name their fruit, and XX is unknown.
"ap" is "unknown": a String case matches with equals().

concepts: Switching on null throws NullPointerException unless the switch has a case null label.
A switch on a String compares with equals(), so the match is case-sensitive.
